answer: Cohort co-insurance staking resists sybils: each identity deposits into a shared loss pool anchored to its invite-cohort, and a detected fraud is paid first from the offender's own full stake, then socialized across its cohort's deposits. This threads liability back to whoever vouched the fakes in, so admitting a thousand onyx-cold identities exposes each co-signer's capital to every sibling's misbehavior. An honest agent anchors one deposit and bears only its own tiny shared risk. Precondition: cohorts are recorded on-ledger so socialized loss has an unforgeable membership.
